newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - Slight distillate build seen in APIs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Slight distillate build seen in APIs.

text.p: Tuesday evening's oil inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) is expected to show a minor build in distillate stocks due to high output in the U.S. Gulf slightly outpacing increased demand.

"Production is high, and with a big Gulf Coast distillate build last week, there will be plenty of distillate heading up to the Northeast," said Linda Abramo, analyst with Energy Security Analysis Inc.
A Reuters average of trader estimates shows distillate stocks up 500,000 barrels for the week ended November 29.

"There could be a draw (in distillate stocks) just on the basis of the weather," said Warren Tashnek, vice president of Fimat USA Futures. Demand for distillates, which is comprised of heating oil and diesel, increased in November due to colder weather in many U.S. regions.

Forecasts for distillate stocks ranged from down two million to up three million barrels. Crude stocks were seen flat to up one million barrels as imports may have increased from a week ago. Gasoline stock forecasts ranged between a draw of one million to up three million. The bias toward a build was due to output at a frenzied 7.8 million barrels.
However, there could be a draw in gasoline stocks due to strong demand in the cash markets, traders said.
With refineries rapidly pumping heating oil and gasoline, runs are seen remaining at 93.7 percent.
Distillate output was a high 3.6 million barrels for the week ended November 22, but in the U.S. Northeast, the world's largest heating oil market, distillate stocks fell that week.
"They may show a build (in the data) this week," said Energy Security analyst Abramo of distillate stocks in the Northeast.

Abramo said there is plenty of distillate barrels in the U.S. Gulf to ship through the huge Colonial Pipeline to the northeast region. In the most recent API data, distillate stocks were up 2.2 million barrels in the U.S. Gulf region.

Historical data also buttresses the argument for a distillate build in this evening's data. Jim Ritterbusch, a trader with Sweeney Oil, said distillate stocks have increased nine out of the last 10 years at an average rate of 1.5 million barrels in the last week of November.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
